title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of Grothendieck's crystalline scribbles. It is a typed, duplicated page numbered '- 65 -' from a lecture course on holomorphic functions with values in a Banach space. It was evidently reused as scrap paper; the handwritten '20' at the lower left is the archive's page count. The surrounding pages (19 and 21) are handwritten notes on Dieudonné/crystalline theory of p-divisible groups: filtrations on Δ(M), Hodge filtration sequences and descent from X_cris to X_zar. This page has nothing to do with them.

Content of the page:

(1) Proposition 2, Schwarz lemma for Banach-valued maps. Let f be holomorphic on a domain A ⊂ C containing the closed unit disc, with a zero of order k at 0, and let M = max_{|z|=1} ||f(z)||. Then ||f(z)|| ≤ M|z|^k for |z| ≤ 1.
- Proof: g(z) = z^{-k} f(z) is holomorphic on A.
- On |z| = 1 we have ||g|| = ||f||, so max ||g|| on the circle is M.
- The maximum principle for vector-valued holomorphic maps gives ||g|| ≤ M on the disc. This principle follows from the scalar case via Hahn–Banach: ||g(z)|| = sup over functionals λ with ||λ|| ≤ 1 of |λ∘g(z)|.

(2) Section 6, equicontinuous sets of holomorphic functions. Proposition 3: let A ⊂ C^p be a domain and Φ a family of holomorphic maps A → E (E a Banach space), uniformly bounded on every compact subset. Then Φ is equicontinuous.
- Fix a in A and a closed polydisc P with centre a and polyradius ρ, contained in A, with ||f|| ≤ M on P for all f in Φ.
- Let Q be the polydisc with centre a and radii ρ/2. For x in Q, the polydisc with centre x and radii ρ/2 lies in P.
- The Cauchy estimates (formula (5) of §3) then give ||∂f/∂x_k(x)|| ≤ M/(ρ/2) = 2M/ρ.
- Integrating df along the segment from a to y gives ||f(y) − f(a)|| ≤ (2pM/ρ)|y − a|, with |·| the sup norm on C^p.
- This is a uniform local Lipschitz bound, hence equicontinuity.

This is the standard first half of Montel's theorem: equicontinuity, then Ascoli. It is presented in a Bourbaki-style course, possibly a course or polycopié by Grothendieck or by someone else; the authorship is unsure.
errors: Typo in the original: 'P un polycylindre fermé de centre a et de rayons ρ, contenu dans P' should read 'contenu dans A'.
Minor: the final estimate uses |y−a| as the sup norm on C^p; the factor p comes from summing the p partial-derivative bounds. This is consistent but not stated explicitly.
The Schwarz-lemma proof tacitly uses the maximum principle for Banach-valued holomorphic functions (via Hahn–Banach). It is standard, and presumably established earlier in the text.

ideas.what: Schwarz lemma (zero of order k) for holomorphic functions with values in a Banach space
ideas.modern_name: Vector-valued Schwarz lemma / maximum modulus principle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schwarz (scalar case, 19th c.); vector-valued versions are folklore (Dunford, Hille, 1930s–50s)
ideas.where_published: Standard in analysis texts (e.g. Cartan's 'Théorie élémentaire des fonctions analytiques'); unsure whether this exact course is Grothendieck's

ideas.what: Locally uniformly bounded families of Banach-valued holomorphic maps on domains in C^p are equicontinuous, via Cauchy estimates on polydiscs
ideas.modern_name: Montel's theorem (equicontinuity part), several complex variables, vector-valued
ideas.usually_credited_to: Montel (1907/1912); several-variable and vector-valued versions are standard
ideas.where_published: Standard textbook material; unsure about provenance of this typescript

deep.surprise_reason: A typed page of a standard course on holomorphic functions (Schwarz lemma, Montel-type equicontinuity), reused as scrap paper among crystalline-cohomology notes. It is entirely textbook material, with no connection to the handwritten mathematics on neighbouring pages.
transcription_corrections: 'contenu dans P' is what the typescript says, but the intended word is 'A' (a typo in the original), so it should not be marked [?].
Handwritten '20' at the bottom left is the archive page number, not part of the text.
'majora-tions' is hyphenated across a line break in the original.
